title: Unregistered Land — Adverse Possession

sections.heading: What this means
sections.content: This land does not appear on the HM Land Registry's record of freehold titles. That does not mean it has no owner — it means the owner has not registered it, and their details are not publicly available. Ownership is evidenced only by paper title deeds, which may exist but are lost or unknown.

sections.heading: Can you claim it?
sections.content:
You may be able to apply for ownership through a legal process called adverse possession. To do this, you must:

1. Occupy the land openly and continuously for 12 years without the owner's consent.
2. Treat it as your own — for example, by fencing it, maintaining it, or building on it.
3. Exclude all others, including any would-be owner, during this period.

After 12 years, you can apply to HM Land Registry to register the land in your name using Form ADV1.

sections.heading: Honest caveats
sections.content:
Important things to understand before you proceed:

- The 12-year clock does not start until you begin occupation. If you have already been maintaining this land, keep records of when you started.
- If an owner produces paper title deeds at any point during or after your 12 years, your claim will fail.
- If the land is owned by the Crown, a government body, or a spiritual corporation (such as a church), the required period is 30 years, not 12.
- This process is not a purchase — there is no payment to a seller. Your legal costs are your main expense.

sections.heading: Estimated cost
sections.content: Legal costs vary. You do not legally need a solicitor to make an adverse possession application, but it is strongly recommended. Typical solicitor fees range from £300 to £1,500 for an uncontested claim. If the application is contested, costs can be significantly higher. HM Land Registry charges a registration fee based on the estimated value of the land (see current fee schedule at gov.uk/government/publications/registration-services-fees).

sections.heading: Your next steps
sections.content:
1. Verify that this land is unregistered using the HMLR Index Map Search (£3 per search): https://www.gov.uk/search-property-information-land-registry
2. Begin occupying and documenting the land. Photograph it regularly with a date-stamped camera or phone. Keep a written diary of maintenance activities.
3. Seek legal advice from a solicitor experienced in property and adverse possession before committing to a 12-year process. Citizens Advice can help you find free or low-cost legal advice: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk
4. When 12 years have elapsed, complete Form ADV1 and submit it to HM Land Registry with your supporting evidence.

sections.heading: Confidence statement
sections.content: Confidence: High — that this land is unregistered. Low — that a claim will succeed. The outcome of any adverse possession application depends on evidence, the behaviour of any owner who appears, and the specific circumstances of the land.

confidence_statement: High — that this land is unregistered. Low — that a claim will succeed.
